claim: Mc Mahon Construction is based in Kilkenny and conducts most of its business in Kilkenny & surrounding counties.
We as a company value the need for training, in order to keep one step ahead of new regulations and building practices.
We have used a number of air to water heat pump units.
We have worked with various green insulation such as sheep's wool and wood fibre insulation etc.
All waste is disposed of appropriately by a licensed haulier.
Efforts are made to recycle material wherever possible.
We enforce a clean site rule, for efficient work practice & safety on site. Each sub contractor must also adhere to this policy.
We are a building firm that specialize in architecturally designed houses that have a strong attention to detail.
We have worked with a number of the architects in the south east.
We have carried out a number of renovations of older houses and cottages.
We have been able to replaster in the traditional lime renders, replace and make good to existing stonework, salvage roofs in poor condition and bring them back to their former glory.
We have refurbished offices, so that they meet the needs of clients.
We use the most up to date telecommunications networks & energy efficient lighting, heating and ventilation systems [in office refurbishments].
We have been involved in a number of conservation projects.
Conservation project: Roth House Kilkenny, first phase to the Third House.
Conservation project: Callan Church internal works.
Conservation project: Coolmore House Thomastown.

We have professional trades men as part of our team, who have plenty of experience in using traditional building methods involving stone work, lime rendering, natural slates & lead work, panelling etc.
Many of our sub contractors have worked with us for 10 years or more.

claim: We have an electrical contractor who has worked with us on various projects over the last 10 years.
Our [electrical] contractor can advise at drawing stage of a lighting layout (mood lighting, levels of light, dimmers, security lights, intercom, surround sound, lighting and socket layouts).
We are approved installers of SIGA airtight membranes and tapes.
We have been on training courses to up skill our team in [air tightness].
We have achieved an airtightness test level of 0.753 m3/(h.m2) @ 50 Pa on new concrete block built house.
The current building regulations (Technical Guidance Documents part L) have a maximum upper limit of 5 m3/(h.m2) @ 50 Pa.
Best practice in domestic dwellings calls for an ac/h rate of not more than 3.0 (natural ventilation), 1.5 (mechanical ventilation, HRU), 0.6 (passive house standard).
SIGA are world leaders in air tightness to buildings.
U valves [sic] of 0.15 W/m2 can be achieved to external walls or lower if required; equally low levels of .013 to attic and floors at affordable prices.

We have being [sic] involved with all of these types of [wall insulation] construction (cavity, cavity with thermal board, timber frame with cellulose, timber frame with block outer skin) and can provide our opinions.
We have used [heat recovery] units on a number of projects.
Heat recovery units (HRU) become efficient when an air tightness of less than 1.5 ac/h is achieved.
A BER rating goes from A1 most efficient to E least efficient.
The BER covers energy use for space heating, water heating, ventilation & lighting, and is calculated on the basis of a standard occupancy using a DEAP calculation.
